claims.claim_text: Products intended for long service lives require written commitments from component suppliers that a part will still be supported ten to fifteen years out; obtaining such letters from semiconductor vendors is difficult but possible.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to guarantee 10, 15 year
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An aftermarket industry exists specifically to keep obsolete semiconductors available for long-life programmes, with Rochester Electronics as an example of a company built on that need.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's actually businesses built upon that
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Component search is a dominant cost in electronic design; a designer may spend the bulk of a project's hours moving between distributor catalogues looking for suitable parts, which motivated EDA vendors to embed distributor stock and pricing lookups directly in schematic tools.
claims.quote_verbatim: 90% of my time often I'll just spend searching
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor lead times of thirty to forty weeks followed the fab shutdowns of the 2008-2009 downturn, because restarting mothballed capacity is slow.
claims.quote_verbatim: 30 weeks, 40 weeks
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: High-volume design requires selecting parts that have a second and third source; a pin-compatible alternative from another vendor is what keeps a product shippable when the primary supplier stops delivering.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to have parts that have to choose parts that have a second source and a third source
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Companies buying components directly from Asian online dealers staff the function with a Mandarin speaker who negotiates in chat and voice, rather than relying on English-language sales channels.
claims.quote_verbatim: we've got a guy who speaks Mandarin
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Open Hardware and The Creative Economy

claims.claim_text: Component engineering - finding, comparing and qualifying parts - can consume eighty to ninety percent of the engineering hours on a new design.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's where you can spend 80 or 90% of your time easily
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Sample requests are often routed through a local distributor who requires the project name, intended volumes and contact details before releasing parts, and follows up with sales calls.
claims.quote_verbatim: You go through a local distributor and they want to know all your details
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: LED Designs, Last Minute Designs and Board Designs

claims.claim_text: Designing a board entirely from free samples is a known trap: the parts obtained as samples may be obscure devices that cannot be purchased in production quantities, leaving a working prototype that cannot be built.
claims.quote_verbatim: But can you get them when you go into production?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: LED Designs, Last Minute Designs and Board Designs

claims.claim_text: Assembly houses require excess components beyond the board count because parts are lost when a reel is loaded and during placement; supplying exactly one reel of one hundred resistors for one hundred boards will not produce one hundred boards.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't give your manufacturer a reel of 100 resistors and expect them to populate 100 boards
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar Cells, SparkFun, TSMC - The Detroit Debunking

claims.claim_text: Mouser ships from a distribution centre near Dallas, so orders placed with the cheapest ground service still arrive next day across much of the United States; shipping speed, availability and price are the three axes on which distributors are chosen.
claims.quote_verbatim: they are overnight shipping. Even if you pay for ground, they're located up near Dallas
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Keyzer - Comical Keyzer Comes a-Callin'

claims.claim_text: A vendor can offer an excellent free-sample service and still be unable to supply production volumes; parts that were trivially obtained as samples turned out to carry forty-week production lead times.
claims.quote_verbatim: They had the best sample service in the business
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: BASIC, Chip companies & Robots - Pernicious Projects, Puppies in Peril

claims.claim_text: Some companies impose a blanket engineering rule forbidding the use of a particular manufacturer's parts, enforced by purchasing rather than by design review, when that manufacturer has repeatedly failed to deliver production volumes.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was actually a blanket rule at many big companies
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: BASIC, Chip companies & Robots - Pernicious Projects, Puppies in Peril

claims.claim_text: Selecting the highest-volume version of a commodity part lets a small buyer ride the pricing and availability created by large buyers, bringing capacitors down to fractions of a cent.
claims.quote_verbatim: I always try and find highest volume parts
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Manufacturer web stores frequently accept an order and take payment without showing stock levels, only disclosing months later that the part is unavailable; distributor listings that expose live stock are safer for committing a design.
claims.quote_verbatim: they don't tell you if they've got stock or not
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Chinese factories and component suppliers shut for roughly two weeks around Chinese New Year; orders placed just before the break are accepted but not shipped until production resumes.
claims.quote_verbatim: A lot of companies are shutting down for, like, almost two weeks
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Alibaba functions as a Chinese component sourcing marketplace aggregating many suppliers rather than as an auction site, filling a role analogous to a Western catalogue distributor.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's a Chinese component sourcing website
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The risk carried by a grey-market or unbranded Chinese component scales with how hard the part is to verify: an LED can be checked by powering it, whereas confirming that a microcontroller is genuine and in-spec is far harder.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it's an LED, your test is, does it turn on?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Grey-market stock is often genuine rather than counterfeit: a contract manufacturer left with part of a reel after a build cannot use it once its date code has aged, and sells the remainder into the secondary market.
claims.quote_verbatim: they had a reel of 3,000 left at the end
claims.speaker: Bunnie Huang
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bunnie Huang - Bunnie's Bibelot Bonification

claims.claim_text: The grey market will break reels, selling a thousand pieces off a three-thousand-piece reel measured out by length, at prices such as eight cents apiece; brokered parts carry no guarantee of provenance.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's no guarantee to them
claims.speaker: Bunnie Huang
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bunnie Huang - Bunnie's Bibelot Bonification

claims.claim_text: Component pricing depends on the buying relationship as well as the quantity on a single line: a customer taking a thousand different reels from one supplier is priced differently from one taking a single high-volume reel.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's also if you're buying, you know, a thousand different reels from the same company at very high volume
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A designer phoning a vendor for volume pricing without a purchase history will not receive a real quote; obtaining genuine volume prices is the work of a full-time purchasing person with established vendor contacts.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's where a full-time purchasing person with all the contacts and the trust with the various vendors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The Canton Fair operates at a scale of roughly 210,000 buyers attending to source components and finished goods, illustrating how much industrial purchasing runs through Chinese trade events.
claims.quote_verbatim: The trade show had 210,000 buyers
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Loading a bill of materials into a single distributor's BOM tool converts reordering into a single transaction with correct part numbers and quantities; the price premium of buying everything from one stocking distributor buys back the time and the certainty.
claims.quote_verbatim: here's the advantage of being able and buying all the parts from the one supplier
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: A single-sourced part with a three-month lead time can force a board respin purely for supply reasons, with no change in the electrical requirement.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're single sourced and you can't second source that sucker and you're stuck with a three-month lead time
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: A second source need not be a different manufacturer: a higher-grade or higher-priced variant from the same vendor, in the same package, can serve as the substitute that keeps a build moving.
claims.quote_verbatim: second source doesn't necessarily mean a different manufacturer
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: Buying the schematic and parts list of a high-volume consumer product, obtainable for a few dollars in the Shenzhen markets, is a deliberate technique for identifying components that are cheap and plentiful because a large manufacturer is already buying them.
claims.quote_verbatim: he bought an iPhone schematic for $4 on the streets of Shenzhen
claims.speaker: Larry Sears
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Larry Sears - Hexagram Hardware Holism

claims.claim_text: Poor component selection early in a programme can strand it: on a military project the prototype hardware could not be rebuilt because the specified parts were no longer obtainable, and the design could not be revisited within the schedule.
claims.quote_verbatim: we can't get the parts anymore because the previous designer designed it poorly
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Distribution, Wozniak & Robots - Early Eight-bit Endgame

claims.claim_text: Western distributor catalogues list every part but do not indicate which parts are commonly used and therefore available at manufacturing scale; that information lives in local markets and Chinese retail sites rather than in the catalogue.
claims.quote_verbatim: which of these parts is common and which of these parts is going to be available on a large scale for manufacturing
claims.speaker: Zach Hoeken
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Hoeken Smith - Creative China Commorant

claims.claim_text: Substituting a locally standard Chinese component for an unusual one specified from a Western catalogue can reduce that line item by an order of magnitude, which is why contract manufacturers return marked-up part lists on a first build.
claims.quote_verbatim: it'll be like a tenth of the cost
claims.speaker: Zach Hoeken
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Hoeken Smith - Creative China Commorant

claims.claim_text: A remote technique for discovering which parts are standard in the Chinese supply chain is to translate the generic component name into Chinese and search Taobao with it, using the relative prominence of listings as a proxy for how common a part is.
claims.quote_verbatim: go to Google Translate, type in ShotKey diode and get the Chinese, paste that into Taobao
claims.speaker: Zach Hoeken
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Hoeken Smith - Creative China Commorant

claims.claim_text: Huaqiangbei in Shenzhen is the world's largest wholesale component market, with thousands of stalls spread over six floors of some twenty buildings; the market is organised for manufacturers but is open to individual buyers.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's thousands of little stands covering six floors of 20 buildings
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Lesnet - Bus Buccaneer Builder

claims.claim_text: A contract manufacturer that cannot source the exact specified part locally may import it instead, paying duties and returning an unexpectedly high quote; a quote that looks too expensive is worth querying for exactly this reason.
claims.quote_verbatim: they will sometimes go out of their way to source it from the US
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Lesnet - Bus Buccaneer Builder

claims.claim_text: Designing to a contract manufacturer's standard part library removes part-number negotiation from each build: the customer names the library item rather than a specific manufacturer part, and the assembler already stocks it.
claims.quote_verbatim: We also design according to a standard part list now
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Lesnet - Bus Buccaneer Builder

claims.claim_text: Offshore assemblers substitute components without notice unless supervised, so a customer moving production overseas must police the bill of materials continuously.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll substitute components in
claims.episode_title: eReaders, datasheets & board assembly - Yearly Yeasty Yapping

claims.claim_text: Availability churn drives schematic rework: a DC-DC converter available two months earlier may be gone while a previously unavailable alternative has returned, so revisiting a bill of materials means re-searching for cost and availability across distributors.
claims.quote_verbatim: This DC to DC converter is not available anymore
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Layout, CAD & Raspberry Pi - Kedogenous Kinetic Knowledge

claims.claim_text: Component pricing tracks how badly the buyer needs the part, so telling a vendor that a design is committed to their device removes the buyer's leverage; disclosing a full production bill of materials has this cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: the price is not dependent on anything other than, you know, how bad you need that part
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Hardware, Surveys and Giveaways - Radular Rental Ranting

claims.claim_text: Vendors increasingly release parts in unique footprints, which makes a competing device a board respin rather than a drop-in and so hardens the single-source position.
claims.quote_verbatim: how all these vendors are moving to unique footprints
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Hardware, Surveys and Giveaways - Radular Rental Ranting

claims.claim_text: A workable part-selection procedure is to start from a vendor application note for the same function, take the part it specifies, then use a distributor's parametric search for similar parts sorted by price.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can always go to a distributor and sort by price
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGAs, Robots & Thermocouples - Wampum's Wavering Worth

claims.claim_text: If every part meeting a set of specifications costs about the same, the price is being set by the specification rather than by the choice of vendor, which is a signal to re-examine whether the specification is really required.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need to look at your application more and see if you actually need the specs that you think you're asking for
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGAs, Robots & Thermocouples - Wampum's Wavering Worth

claims.claim_text: A broker sits between the buyer and an unknown upstream source, so the buyer cannot see where the parts came from; most brokered transactions deliver good parts and the occasional one does not.
claims.quote_verbatim: You're buying through the broker and then they get from wherever source of the source
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with the SparkFun Team - Efficacious Engineering Ensemble

claims.claim_text: A broker with a legitimate-looking website that passes casual diligence and even delivers a first order can still be a fraud that disappears afterwards; the failure mode is not detectable from the web presence.
claims.quote_verbatim: the company just disappeared off the face of the earth
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with the SparkFun Team - Efficacious Engineering Ensemble

claims.claim_text: In-house buyers act as a design gate, rejecting parts that cannot be obtained in the required annual volume regardless of how well the design works.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's no way we can get 10,000 of those within a year
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with the SparkFun Team - Efficacious Engineering Ensemble

claims.claim_text: Small buyers face a structural penalty at the boundary between catalogue and reel quantities: buying single reels from a catalogue distributor costs more than the local supplier price available to someone taking twenty reels.
claims.quote_verbatim: you end up buying from DigiKey and paying more than what you get it from your local supplier at if you bought 20 reels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Troubleshooting, PCBs and LEDs - Quaintized Quich Quelling

claims.claim_text: A bill of materials is only de-risked when each critical line has a second source and a stated fallback, including for mechanical and specialty items whose single supplier could vanish or reprice.
claims.quote_verbatim: You never want to do anything where you're only single source
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Intense Illusion Introduction

claims.claim_text: Chip vendors deliberately use specialised footprints, so many modern devices are effectively single-sourced by construction and a supply failure forces a new board rather than a substitution.
claims.quote_verbatim: The chip vendors want it that way. So it's almost by design single sourced
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Intense Illusion Introduction

claims.claim_text: Long-lead parts must be bought before a crowdfunding campaign opens rather than after it closes; a single reel purchased in advance for about four thousand two hundred dollars is the price of being able to fulfil on the promised schedule.
claims.quote_verbatim: I just paid 4,200 bucks for a reel of bloody components
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Forty-week lead times were normal for semiconductors in the early 1990s, and shortages since have pushed typical lead times back towards twenty-eight weeks and beyond.
claims.quote_verbatim: 40 weeks was a typical lead time
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Precision components are held in stock by almost nobody, so a design using them requires the developer to buy up most of the available world supply in advance and carry thousands of dollars of inventory before any revenue arrives.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm using really expensive precision resistors in here that hardly anyone holds in stock
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: Minimum order quantities dictate step changes in cost: parts not stocked in one-off quantities must be bought by the reel, so an extra thousand units of product can require an extra thousand-piece reel at four dollars a part.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have to buy an extra reel of 1,000 components at $4 a pop
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Discussing Innovation and the Future with Mike Ossmann - Fiesty Festivus Futurology

claims.claim_text: Swapping in an electrically identical part from a different manufacturer should still be recorded against the build, because lot-to-lot differences must remain traceable to the units they went into.
claims.quote_verbatim: you should notate that in some way because then if there are lot differences
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: High-end CAD tools carry approved alternative parts against each bill of materials line, which lets purchasing pick whichever qualified device is available in a given week without returning to engineering.
claims.quote_verbatim: the purchasing people can chew, they're free to choose whichever part is available this week
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Catalogue distributors are chosen over local suppliers for small builds because stock levels and backorder dates are visible and no negotiation or quotation cycle is needed, even though the unit price is higher.
claims.quote_verbatim: You don't have to talk to a human
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An obsolescence can arrive with no last-time-buy window at all, leaving a manufacturer to purchase the remaining world stock; where the part defines a platform that other modules plug into, substitution breaks compatibility with everything already shipped.
claims.quote_verbatim: There was no last buy
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: When a platform-defining part goes obsolete and no drop-in exists, one remedy is to commission a manufacturer to copy the original design and produce a compatible device.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had to go find a manufacturer who was willing to copy that existing design and manufacture us a compatible one
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding platforms differ in when cash reaches the creator: some release funds as the target is met, while others hold the money for about two weeks after the campaign ends, which delays part purchasing and is a common cause of late hardware delivery.
claims.quote_verbatim: They put the money on hold for two weeks and then it comes through
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Chris Becomes Self Employed - Quixotic Quitting Quaere

claims.claim_text: Industry practice favours established parts from large manufacturers, because a sole device from a smaller or restructuring vendor can be cancelled and leave a shipping product with no replacement.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's so important when you work in the industry to pick established parts
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Chairs, Sparks and Devices - Optional Olent Obreption

claims.claim_text: Sourcing must be designed in rather than delegated: a turnkey assembler or fulfilment partner cannot repair a bill of materials that was never checked for availability.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't just leave it up to your turnkey assembler
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Spacing Out On Space - Dave's Dongle Designing

claims.claim_text: Buying critical parts up front on behalf of an assembler preempts the delay between contract signature and their purchasing department placing the order, during which stock can disappear.
claims.quote_verbatim: by the time they do that, oops, sorry, that, that, that parts out of stock
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Spacing Out On Space - Dave's Dongle Designing

claims.claim_text: Before catalogue distribution reached worldwide one-off quantities, parts were bought through a manufacturer's local representative network with account paperwork and bank payment; current-generation devices are now listed at reasonable single-piece prices from the day of release.
claims.quote_verbatim: you had to buy them directly from Texas Instruments or some other company
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: B Plus Boards and D Minus Cities - Uneath Urban Ubication

claims.claim_text: A lead time quoted by a distributor is often matched by the manufacturer, so escalating to the factory does not necessarily shorten it; a two-month wait on a single critical resistor can hold up an entire product reorder.
claims.quote_verbatim: That critical resistor you need is two months lead time
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: An unusually low distributor price can be a signal that stock is being cleared ahead of end-of-life rather than a bargain, so price alone is an unreliable basis for designing a part in.
claims.quote_verbatim: what if it's low price because they're trying to unload stock right now
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor manufacturers schedule production from demand statistics on each part number, so a device with declining order history drops out of the build plan and reappears as a long lead time for whoever is still using it.
claims.quote_verbatim: if they're seeing the trend down on that part, it's not going to sit into their schedule
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: Contract manufacturers keep a house parts library of components they continuously restock and preload; designing to that library lowers cost because no new procurement is required for the build.
claims.quote_verbatim: they can optimize cost if you start to use certain parts, basically, because they have them on the shelf
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Last Minute Decisions - Obdurate Onepercenter Obstacles

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor allocation follows revenue: engineering support and supply are directed at the largest customers, so a design consuming a few thousand parts is served after those consuming millions.
claims.quote_verbatim: all of the resources taken up by these big companies with the big top line dollars
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Space Bound, Again - Xtreme Xtraplanetary Xenonosocomiophobia

claims.claim_text: International courier shipments of components can sit in customs clearance for weeks without notification, so transit time on an imported reel is not the same as the courier's quoted service level.
claims.quote_verbatim: my parts have been sitting in customs in DHL in Sydney since the 4th of December
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Supply Chain Woes And Wares - Nonplussed Neotechnic Nithing

claims.claim_text: A turnkey build of a simple fifteen-component board through an overseas assembler took about two months end to end including quotation cycles and shipping, with the Chinese New Year shutdown adding further delay.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's two months right there
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: Very large buyers commit cash to multi-year purchases of chip and fab output, which removes that capacity from the market for everyone else.
claims.quote_verbatim: They buy up like five year stocks worth of chips
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Compare and Contrast Tech Entitlement - Worldly Working Wonks

claims.claim_text: Shipping costs often erase the savings from splitting a bill of materials across distributors to chase the lowest unit price, since a few cents saved on a line item can be swamped by an eight-dollar or fifty-dollar carriage charge.
claims.quote_verbatim: but it's eight bucks in shipping
claims.speaker: Chris Church
claims.episode_title: An interview with Macrofab - Macro Manufacturing Mechanization

claims.claim_text: One-time-programmable devices must be programmed before assembly, so they cannot be ordered by the assembler in the normal flow and have to be supplied to the build already programmed.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a one-time programmable chip. So they had to be sent to us pre-programmed
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An interview with Macrofab - Macro Manufacturing Mechanization

claims.claim_text: House parts and market parts cross over as volume rises: an assembler's stocked house part can be cheaper in small quantities while a market part saves a few cents a board once volumes reach the low thousands, so the comparison has to be made at the intended build quantity.
claims.quote_verbatim: a house part may be cheaper at a very low volume, but a particular market part, once you get to 1,000 units, that one actually saves you $0.03 a board
claims.speaker: Chris Church
claims.episode_title: An interview with Macrofab - Macro Manufacturing Mechanization

claims.claim_text: Component manufacturers will help an assembler obtain distributor discounts in exchange for that assembler stocking a hard-to-find part as a standing house part, because a stocked part gets designed in.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you guys are willing to carry that, we'll, we'll, we'll help you get a discount on this part from this distributor over here
claims.speaker: Chris Church
claims.episode_title: An interview with Macrofab - Macro Manufacturing Mechanization

claims.claim_text: Before online catalogue ordering, European distributors such as Farnell and RS were far more expensive in real terms and required a corporate credit account, which is why component hoards accumulated by individual engineers were valuable.
claims.quote_verbatim: you had to have a corporate account with them
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Robots are coming - Ominous Operational Overhaul

claims.claim_text: Component availability is geographically determined: an engineer in Yugoslavia had to travel a thousand kilometres to Munich to buy parts that are now purchasable locally.
claims.quote_verbatim: I had to travel to Munich 1,000 kilometers
claims.speaker: Voja Antonic
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Voja Antonic - Gerontogenous Galaksija Genesis

claims.claim_text: Shipping components into countries outside the main distribution networks carries disproportionate cost and delay: three dollars of cable delivered to Chile cost two hundred and fifty dollars, sat three days in customs and attracted import tax, with a week as the fastest achievable transit.
claims.quote_verbatim: that was $3 worth of cables and it was $250 and it stayed in customs for three days
claims.speaker: Greg Gage
claims.episode_title: An interview with Greg and Tim of Backyard Brains - Boethetic Bug Brainwaves

claims.claim_text: Setting a crowdfunding price before the board is built and before any component pricing has been negotiated with vendors is a structural way to underprice a product, because the bill of materials is not yet known.
claims.quote_verbatim: we didn't have anything pre-negotiated with any of the vendors on the board
claims.speaker: Andreas Olofsson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Andreas Olofsson - Adapteva's Ampliative Abacus

claims.claim_text: Once a component is purchasable from a catalogue distributor it carries little supply-chain differentiation, since any competitor can obtain the same parts; the differentiation of a product built entirely from catalogue parts has to lie elsewhere.
claims.quote_verbatim: by the time you can buy it on DigiKey, it's almost commodity
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Farnell, Element 14 and Newark are regional brands of the same distribution group, which serves the United Kingdom and much of Europe from a central hub.
claims.quote_verbatim: Farnell, Element 14, Newark, that's all kind of the same thing
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ronald Sousa of Hash Define Electronics

claims.claim_text: A part chosen for its feature set can turn out to have no pin- or package-compatible relatives within its own family, leaving the design locked to one orderable device with no substitution path.
claims.quote_verbatim: you buy the unicorn part, and you can never swap it in
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Designing around interchangeable functional blocks specified only by their interface lowers supply risk but sharply raises the design and qualification effort, because every candidate part must be accommodated.
claims.quote_verbatim: that lowers your risk for a lot of stuff. But that increases the hassle factor like 100x
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Distributor stock checked one day can be zero the next, replaced by a twelve-week lead time, so availability verified during design is not availability at the moment of ordering.
claims.quote_verbatim: They were in stock in DigiKey yesterday, but you went to press the order button today and the stock is zero
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Replacing an obsolete discrete semiconductor typically means working down a chain of increasingly marginal sources: catalogue distributors first, then specialist obsolete-part manufacturers, then brokers.
claims.quote_verbatim: a fly-by-night obsolete transistor manufacturer
claims.speaker: Mark Morin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mark Morin of Nufern

claims.claim_text: A paper catalogue can surface a substitution that a parametric search will not, because unrelated part families appear on the same page; a mobile phone SIM connector costing tens of pence was used as a sprung surface-mount contact in place of a spring probe.
claims.quote_verbatim: this is one of these cases where a paper catalog is great because you see stuff on the same page
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: A single project can consume the world stock of a specific part number: roughly thirty thousand connectors were bought out across several distributors, which leaves any concurrent user of that part with nothing.
claims.quote_verbatim: we actually cleared out pretty much the entire worldwide stock of those
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Live from Serbia with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: A large wireless semiconductor vendor refused to open an account or provide field applications engineering support without a commitment of around 250,000 units per year, which places its parts out of reach of a startup at the design stage.
claims.quote_verbatim: unless you can commit to 250 000 units per year
claims.speaker: Omer Kilic

claims.claim_text: Established buyers can obtain a part recommendation and ready-made CAD libraries from a vendor's field engineers within days, a channel that startups without volume commitments do not have, so their part selection and library work is done unaided.
claims.quote_verbatim: sourcing components i'm very familiar with this
claims.speaker: Omer Kilic

claims.claim_text: The practical knowledge of manufacturing and sourcing - data packs, standardised bills of materials, how to deal with contract manufacturers - is transmitted informally rather than taught, which is a systematic gap for first-time hardware builders.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's it's folklore um you don't get taught this at school
claims.speaker: Omer Kilic

claims.claim_text: A distributor endorsement badge on a crowdfunding campaign reduces to a check that the listed parts can be obtained, and does not cover design, mechanical tooling or delivery risk.
claims.quote_verbatim: All they do is look over their bill of materials and go, yep, we can get those parts for you
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Many companies presenting themselves as component or subassembly suppliers are middlemen rather than manufacturers, which limits how far a buyer can develop the technical partnership or pricing they expect.
claims.quote_verbatim: one of many middlemen
claims.speaker: Zach Dunham

claims.claim_text: Component manufacture co-located with assembly in China allows a build to be scaled within days in a way that ordering from a Western catalogue distributor cannot match.
claims.quote_verbatim: In China, they make the components for the thing you're building right next to the thing you're building
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: An interview with Alvaro and Jen from the URE Podcast

claims.claim_text: Engineering has been described as the art of building something with the parts you can actually obtain, which makes availability a first-order design constraint rather than a procurement detail.
claims.quote_verbatim: engineering is the art of building something with stuff you can get
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Distributor stock has a hard boundary: the unit beyond the quantity in distribution has to be ordered from the manufacturer, which brings factory lead times and minimum order quantities into play, so a quotation should be obtained at the intended build volume early in the design.
claims.quote_verbatim: 800 number 801 means you have to order from the manufacturer and then you are dealing with lead times and minimum order quantities
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Many listed suppliers do not hold stock at all: identical quantities appearing across several websites indicate that the same underlying inventory at a large distributor is being resold, with the order passed upstream on receipt.
claims.quote_verbatim: they don't hold stock
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Distribution has consolidated into a few groups, with Avnet owning the Farnell and Element 14 brands and Arrow operating several brands of its own, so apparently independent sources can share an owner.
claims.quote_verbatim: Avnet owns Farnell Element 14 now
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A quick availability sanity check on a candidate part is to search the part number with the word buy and see whether several independent sources appear; a thin result set signals a sourcing problem before the part is designed in.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can also just type into Google, part number, buy
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Distributors increasingly forward end-of-life and obsolescence notices to customers who have previously bought the affected part, which gives a design owner an early warning channel.
claims.quote_verbatim: when they get an obsolescence notice they'll pass it to people who've bought stuff
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A shipping bill of materials should be re-run against distributor availability every few months, since re-quoting is what surfaces a part that has quietly become unobtainable.
claims.quote_verbatim: run your bomb every couple months make sure they can actually buy the parts
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Designing in an obscure part carries two compounding penalties: it is more likely to be discontinued as its customer count falls, and during an allocation its users are at the back of the queue with no distribution stock to buy through.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no way to fast forward by buying out of distribution

claims.claim_text: Shortage reports stated as a blanket claim that a distributor is out of a whole component class are usually false in general but true for specific case sizes and voltage ratings, alongside higher prices, so the response is to re-specify rather than to give up.
claims.quote_verbatim: Searching for a certain size and voltage, it may be true
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Supply readiness for a hardware launch is assessed by whether suppliers are lined up, the supply chain is in place, cash flow is secure and payment terms have been agreed, none of which is normally visible to backers.
claims.quote_verbatim: have you lined up all your suppliers is your supply chain in place
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Distributor margins on volume lines are thinner than assumed: a five-thousand-piece reel bought directly from the semiconductor manufacturer's own web store costs about the same as the same reel from a catalogue distributor, because distribution agreements hold the prices together.
claims.quote_verbatim: I want a reel of 5,000 parts. It's going to cost me. Say. $5,000. I go to DigiKey. It's practically the same cost
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Cut-tape and small-quantity handling at a catalogue distributor is effectively a loss leader against the volume business, since the labour of cutting a strip off a reel and bagging it is not covered by the line price.
claims.quote_verbatim: Some of that stuff is loss leader anyways
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Manufacturer-direct stores price-match catalogue distributors rather than undercutting them, because both parties want to hold margin, so buying direct is not automatically cheaper.
claims.quote_verbatim: They're trying to price match as high as they can
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A reseller showing stock may not be holding it: an order that ships several days later indicates the seller is buying it in from elsewhere, unless the seller is the manufacturer.
claims.quote_verbatim: it'll appear like they have it in stock, but then they'll say, you know, oh, it'll take five days to start shipping
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Cut-tape reels sold by catalogue distributors carry a per-reel handling charge and a leader tape, and a pick-and-place setup can consume a large fraction of a small quantity in machine setup, so ordering ten parts on a reel may not yield ten placements.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's why you buy Digi reels and Mouser reels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The traditional quotation flow for a build is to email the bill of materials as a spreadsheet to several distributors and compare the returned prices line by line.
claims.quote_verbatim: You send it off to four different distributors. They're all getting spreadsheets
claims.speaker: Chris Denney

claims.claim_text: Line items are split across distributors only when the saving justifies the extra handling; where the difference is around a hundred dollars, buying the whole bill of materials from one supplier is the better trade.
claims.quote_verbatim: if there's cost savings, you split them out
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Component choice can be dictated purely by which part a distributor holds in sufficient quantity, with electrical selection reduced to whatever LED there is enough stock of.
claims.quote_verbatim: we could only use the stuff that DigiKey had enough stock of
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: The capacitor shortage bit hardest on high-voltage and high-capacitance parts, while commodity values such as 100 nanofarad 0603 remained obtainable at roughly double their previous unit price.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's the high-voltage, high-value ones that are just super, super unobtainium
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Popularity itself creates scarcity: the lowest-end and most widely used microcontroller variants became the hardest to obtain precisely because everybody had designed them in.
claims.quote_verbatim: some of the more popular lowest-end STMs are getting quite hard to get hold of now
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Supplier payment terms function as working capital: net thirty on components let early Apple buy parts, build computers and sell them before the invoice fell due, financing production without capital.
claims.quote_verbatim: would you like a 30-day net
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Most sellers listing components on Chinese marketplaces are trading companies or listing agents rather than the manufacturer, so the party a buyer negotiates with often has no control over the product.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're not the manufacturer, right? It'll, they'll make it look like it. They're like a listing agent
claims.speaker: Joe Long

claims.claim_text: Before online search, sourcing a mechanical or electronic part meant working through printed manufacturer directories such as the Thomas Register and telephoning each listed maker to find who was still in business.
claims.quote_verbatim: You go down the list calling each one to see who's still in business
claims.speaker: Charles Alexanian

claims.claim_text: The marginal cost of the first component on a new board is dominated by fixed costs: once the distributor order, board fabrication and engineering time are counted, putting a single resistor onto a first article runs into thousands of dollars, and turnkey assembly of a first five boards can cost several hundred.
claims.quote_verbatim: to get a single resistor onto a board, it's going to cost a couple thousand dollars
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Large organisations force new components through an internal approval and part-numbering process before they can be used, because at production volume the part must be purchasable, payable and schedulable across multiple approved vendors, not merely electrically correct.
claims.quote_verbatim: This has to go into our system
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A single very large customer buying an entire fab's output can remove a part from the market, which is a supply risk a small company cannot mitigate by ordering earlier.
claims.quote_verbatim: they just buy out the entire fabs worth

claims.claim_text: Internal part numbering decouples a design from its vendors: one company part number for a logic device can map to five approved manufacturers, and purchasing buys against whichever is available without engineering involvement.
claims.quote_verbatim: there will be like five different manufacturers of that 74HC00. And it doesn't matter
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Handing a bill of materials to a local assembler for a box build transfers the sourcing labour as well as the placement work, which for a large bill of materials on a small prototype run is usually cheaper than doing it in house.
claims.quote_verbatim: We just give them the bomb and they'll source everything, assemble them and deliver us four assembled boards
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A design that deliberately uses the most commoditised footprints keeps several manufacturers' parts droppable into the same land pattern, which is achievable for standard logic but not for switching regulators or microcontrollers.
claims.quote_verbatim: I want to be able to, to drop six different parts in the same footprint
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Lead times published on distributor websites are a starting figure rather than a prediction, and parts frequently arrive substantially sooner than the quoted date.
claims.quote_verbatim: the lead times that are on the websites are usually completely wrong in practice
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: During the shortage a working practice was to buy ahead on the assumption that any order might take a full quarter to arrive, keeping enough stock on hand to absorb the delay.
claims.quote_verbatim: I sort of buy with the knowledge that it may take a quarter to actually get the parts
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Component pricing slides materially only above certain volumes, and the very largest semiconductor vendors will not engage below multi-million-unit volumes; buyers below that threshold reach the silicon indirectly through module makers who do have the relationship.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're not moving five million units, like, good luck getting anybody to pick up the phone
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: Smaller semiconductor vendors will work more closely with small customers than large ones will, because they have more to gain from the relationship, which makes vendor size a selection criterion in its own right.
claims.quote_verbatim: smaller chip vendors will maybe work a little bit more closely with smaller companies
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: Some component suppliers will not sell to an individual at all and require a registered company before releasing parts, which is a barrier at the earliest prototype stage.
claims.quote_verbatim: wouldn't even send me the parts unless I was a company
claims.speaker: Christina Cyr

claims.claim_text: A production shock propagates into component availability on a delay: interruptions at a passive component factory do not appear as distributor shortages for weeks, which makes the leading indicators easy to miss.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's not going to hit for a couple of weeks yet
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A purchasing department optimising purely on unit cost can buy grey-market parts that are counterfeit or out of spec; a connector quoted at a tenth of the branded price is the shape of that failure.
claims.quote_verbatim: this $1 connector, we found a source for 10 cents
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Every unique reel on a bill of materials is a separate procurement risk, and a shortfall discovered at the assembly house produces substitution requests mid-build, such as whether a 1K resistor may be fitted in place of a 1.02K.
claims.quote_verbatim: we ran out of 1.02K resistors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Two and a Half Orders of Magnitude

claims.claim_text: Volume arithmetic has to be done before part selection: fifty LEDs on each of fifty thousand boards is two and a half million parts, a quantity available from few sources and carrying a lead time of at least twenty weeks.
claims.quote_verbatim: 50 LEDs times 50,000 boards
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Once parts are ordered at production volume the design is frozen against them, so a late discovery that a device is thermally or electrically unsuitable strands the committed inventory.
claims.quote_verbatim: we've already ordered, you know, half a million parts
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Component distributors have bought into electronics media and search: Arrow acquired EE Times in 2016, and services such as GlobalSpec sit in the component sourcing business alongside FindChips and Octopart.
claims.quote_verbatim: Arrow bought EE Times in 2016
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The historical arrangement was that a chip customised for a large customer was afterwards released to general distribution, so the part eventually became purchasable by anyone; that route has narrowed, leaving devices that never reach open distribution.
claims.quote_verbatim: we'll custom design that for you. But we will then make it available to everyone else
claims.episode_title: Right To Repair with Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: Where a device is only obtainable through informal Chinese sellers, incoming inspection becomes mandatory: parts must be tested before being fitted to a customer's board, because provenance cannot be established any other way.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'll have to test the stuff out before I use it on customers to make sure I got something legitimate
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann
claims.episode_title: Right To Repair with Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: When a device is unavailable in any distribution channel, harvesting it from a new retail assembly that contains it can be the only supply route; charging cases have been bought purely to remove one power management chip.
claims.quote_verbatim: ripping the chip off of it and then throwing it away
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann
claims.episode_title: Right To Repair with Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: Freight and handling overheads dominate small-quantity sourcing: a hundred dollars of shipping on five modules doubles their effective cost, and a seven-dollar per-reel charge across fifty unique parts adds three hundred and fifty dollars to a build.
claims.quote_verbatim: seven bucks per reel doesn't sound that bad in single quantities, but if you have 50 uniques and you need 50 digi reels, that's another 350 bucks
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Camera module vendors treat a million units as a small order, so an order of ten thousand attracts both a high unit price and a lead time of around eighteen weeks; building in batches rather than in one volume order makes the pricing worse again.
claims.quote_verbatim: a small order for those guys are maybe a million cameras
claims.speaker: Brandon Gilles
claims.episode_title: Depth and AI with Brandon Gilles and Brian Weinstein

claims.claim_text: A single small manufacturer can absorb the entire distributor stock of a part, leaving nothing for anyone else, which is one mechanism by which shortages propagate from the bottom of the market.
claims.quote_verbatim: I sucked up the worldwide supply off Mouser and DigiKey
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: The 2020-2021 shortage was amplified by demand-side behaviour: customers cancelled backlogs at the start of the pandemic, then reinstated them within months, and semiconductor capacity had already been reallocated to buyers who never cancelled.
claims.quote_verbatim: pull all the orders, shut everything down. This is 2008 again
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: During an allocation the working rule shifts from designing a part in and buying it later to buying stock at the moment it appears, in the quantity the known build requires.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you see something in stock, you buy it, use that, you buy it right then
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Small Chinese manufacturers of commodity goods build from whatever parts the local market holds at the time, so successive orders of the same model number can differ in both hardware and firmware.
claims.quote_verbatim: the software and the hardware will be completely different because they just use whatever components they can get at the local market
claims.speaker: Big Clive
claims.episode_title: The King of Trash with Big Clive

claims.claim_text: Distributor stock of zero paired with a thirty-two week lead time was a routine state during the shortage, including for simple eight-pin through-hole controller chips, and through-hole single-sided construction remains cheaper than surface mount for some products.
claims.quote_verbatim: zero in stock on DigiKey, unfortunately. Oh, that's 32 week lead time
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Component inventory software tracks what parts are physically held, associates them with builds as they are consumed, and drives purchasing from the resulting shortfall.
claims.quote_verbatim: PartsBox is an app that lets you keep track of your parts inventory
claims.speaker: Jan Rychter

claims.claim_text: Personal or shelf stock becomes a real supply channel during a shortage, with builds completed from parts held outside distribution when nothing can be bought.
claims.quote_verbatim: I couldn't buy something out of distribution and I happened to have some stuff laying around

claims.claim_text: Part equivalence is project-specific rather than absolute: a substitution acceptable on one design may be barred on another by tolerance, temperature coefficient, durability, or a requirement that the part be sourced from a particular country.
claims.quote_verbatim: because of your sourcing requirements that you're supposed to buy stuff only from a certain country
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An assembler's quoted component price should be checked against aggregator listings before a design is changed: a part quoted at three dollars fifty each was available at around a dollar fifty elsewhere, which is cheaper to resolve than a redesign.
claims.quote_verbatim: they were charging like $3.50 for each one of these chips
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Small hardware firms responded to the shortage by buying a year of chips ahead of a production run that had not been scheduled, tying up working capital in inventory for products that might not be built.
claims.quote_verbatim: we might need to buy a year's worth of chips for something we might be doing
claims.speaker: Colin O'Flynn
claims.episode_title: Shouting at chips with Colin O'Flynn

claims.claim_text: Low-cost assembly services only place parts they stock themselves, so a design that mixes stocked and non-stocked components becomes a partial machine build followed by hand assembly of the remainder.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's just whatever parts they stock, which is not everything
claims.speaker: Colin O'Flynn
claims.episode_title: Shouting at chips with Colin O'Flynn

claims.claim_text: Rebranded and house-marked microcontrollers make a product unrepairable in practice, because the replacement device cannot be identified or sourced.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you can't source the chips, it's not repairable
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In precision instruments a substantial part of the value lies in sourcing rather than circuit design: obtaining higher-specification parts than the open market offers, or binning ordinary parts by test, is what produces the published performance.
claims.quote_verbatim: further sourcing of higher specced parts than you could buy on the open market
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Precision parts are single-sourced and carry order-of-magnitude price breaks, with a resistor costing around four dollars in reel quantity against roughly twelve dollars as a single piece, so low-volume production absorbs the difference directly out of margin.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're paying four bucks a resistor instead of maybe the single piece price for one would be like 12 bucks a resistor
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Repeated part substitutions during a shortage drive board revisions on their own: a small product reached its fourth revision purely because components kept becoming unavailable and had to be replaced.
claims.quote_verbatim: I am already at revision D
claims.speaker: Florin of Voltlog
claims.episode_title: YouTube to Consulting with Florin of Voltlog

claims.claim_text: The 2021 shortage reached basic through-hole components, with plain T1-3/4 LEDs taking three to four months to arrive, which distinguished it from earlier years when one backordered part would clear in a couple of weeks.
claims.quote_verbatim: it took about probably three or four months to get those parts
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Panic buying propagates a shortage: a designer who switches platform and then buys three reels of the replacement removes that stock from whoever had planned on it, moving the problem one step down the chain.
claims.quote_verbatim: then I just like bought three reels of the components
claims.speaker: Philip Salmony
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor vendors publish reel price breaks directly, with a 500-piece reel of a microcontroller at eighty cents a unit against seventy cents on a 3,400-piece reel.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can buy 500, a reel of 500 of them for at a unit price of 80 cents, or you can buy a reel of 3,400 for 70 cents
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Supply chain information has traditionally been opaque to design engineers because it is held by a separate purchasing team and consulted weeks or months after the part selection was made.
claims.quote_verbatim: has always been opaque to the engineers
claims.speaker: Michael Corr
claims.episode_title: Product Lifecycle Management with Michael Corr

claims.claim_text: A procurement team cannot substitute an unavailable part on its own authority, so every shortage becomes a context switch back to the engineer to approve, test or re-select, which is a structural inefficiency between design and manufacturing.
claims.quote_verbatim: a procurement person often doesn't have the information required to, on their own, pick an alternative
claims.speaker: Michael Corr
claims.episode_title: Product Lifecycle Management with Michael Corr

claims.claim_text: A functional equivalent to an unavailable part frequently arrives in a different package, so the substitution is a board respin rather than a bill of materials edit, with the cost and delay that implies.
claims.quote_verbatim: even a functional equivalent didn't come in the same package
claims.speaker: Michael Corr
claims.episode_title: Product Lifecycle Management with Michael Corr

claims.claim_text: The distributors familiar to engineers are not the ones used for volume production; suppliers digitising their catalogues and exposing pricing and lead time through APIs is what lets a designer see real availability at the point of part selection.
claims.quote_verbatim: there are many, many other suppliers out there that they just don't have access to and probably would be the ones that are used for final volume production
claims.speaker: Michael Corr
claims.episode_title: Product Lifecycle Management with Michael Corr

claims.claim_text: An overseas cost-down pass does not redesign a circuit; it replaces the specified devices with cheaper equivalents from the local component ecosystem, which then have to be validated against the original specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: They're just finding stuff in the local ecosystem. That's a lot cheaper
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Some manufacturers deliberately restrict their bill of materials to domestically made components and will change a part specifically to keep the sourcing local.
claims.quote_verbatim: they go to extraordinary lengths to find parts made in South Korea
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Chinese-designed commodity interface chips undercut Western equivalents substantially, with a USB-to-serial device listed at 48 cents in one-off quantity against more than 122,000 pieces in stock.
claims.quote_verbatim: 48 cents. 122,000 in stock. One-off price
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Export controls constrain sourcing directly: sanctions blocked Russia and Belarus from buying Taiwanese processors above a clock threshold, and comparable rules govern international distributor purchases.
claims.quote_verbatim: cannot buy any CPU From Taiwan Over 25 meg
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Export regulation can force a manufacturer to cripple a product for foreign markets: thermal cameras above roughly eight or nine frames per second are treated as controlled, so units sold outside the United States are software-limited.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's over 8 frames per second
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The shortage shifted risk tolerance in part selection, making designers willing to qualify unfamiliar Asian silicon and to search Chinese distributors first, where previously they would have defaulted to a known family that was in stock.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm going to LCSC sooner
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In the capacitor shortage of the late 2010s a reel of surface-mount one microfarad capacitors could not be obtained at any price, showing that during a severe allocation money does not substitute for availability.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could not get a reel of SMD, you know, one mic caps to, you know, it didn't matter how much you paid
claims.speaker: Ron Demcko
claims.episode_title: Capacitor Schoopage with Ron Demcko from AVX

claims.claim_text: Distributor inventory counts drift from physical stock as parts are pulled from a tray, so a listed quantity can be met with a cancellation notice when the bin turns out to hold fewer parts than the system believed.
claims.quote_verbatim: they only had 300 in the bin
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Best way to find a leak

claims.claim_text: Brokers price on their ability to find parts rather than on the parts themselves, quoting a fee per thousand pieces on the understanding that a high enough price will surface stock somewhere.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you pay me $12 per thousand, I will find
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: During the shortage nearly all the active devices on a typical hundred-part board became unobtainable while the roughly eighty percent of the bill of materials that is passive stayed available, so the redesign burden concentrated on the ICs and FETs.
claims.quote_verbatim: almost all the ICs and almost all of the FETs you couldn't get
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Buying from the grey market at inflated prices is a rational choice for a company that must ship to make payroll, which is why broker pricing holds during an allocation.
claims.quote_verbatim: pays the ransom and gets them from the gray market
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Through-hole packages of a device sometimes remained available when the surface-mount versions did not, making the older package a legitimate shortage workaround.
claims.quote_verbatim: you should even switch to the dips because those are actually still available
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: In Indian cities components are bought from a dedicated market district of small densely stocked shops, where staff will work through variants with a buyer in person; there is no catalogue or telephone equivalent.
claims.quote_verbatim: in every city that one area where you can go to find components
claims.speaker: Amitabh Shrivastava
claims.episode_title: Refrigerators and Robots with Amitabh Shrivastava

claims.claim_text: Second-hand and surplus mechanical components carry a quality cost that must be tested for: about a quarter of used solenoid valves bought from surplus dealers were unusable and had to be scrapped after fitting.
claims.quote_verbatim: 25% of the valves was just not usable
claims.speaker: Amitabh Shrivastava
claims.episode_title: Refrigerators and Robots with Amitabh Shrivastava

claims.claim_text: Component manufacturers set minimum engagement quantities that exclude small builders: a valve supplier would not discuss an order below two thousand pieces against production runs of one to two hundred, forcing bulk purchase and inventory.
claims.quote_verbatim: they won't even talk to me for anything less than 2000 pieces
claims.speaker: Amitabh Shrivastava
claims.episode_title: Refrigerators and Robots with Amitabh Shrivastava

claims.claim_text: The conservative sourcing rule is to buy only through authorised distributors and avoid consumer marketplaces entirely, with the counter-argument being the price premium that authorised distribution carries.
claims.quote_verbatim: Don't ever buy parts on eBay. Only buy them from the legitimate distributors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Designing to availability inverts the usual order: browse a low-cost distributor sorted by price, assemble a parts budget from what is cheap and stocked, and derive the product from that.
claims.quote_verbatim: You go there and then you sort by price
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A prototype-sized order from a catalogue distributor can be easier than pulling parts off production reels already held in stock, and covered over ninety percent of one bill of materials during the shortage, with the residual being a single instrumentation amplifier.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was easier to order a prototype-sized batch of parts from DigiKey than to pull them off reels
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: A practical substitution search during a shortage means opening every device in a distributor's category listing and checking data sheets for a matching footprint, rather than relying on parametric equivalence.
claims.quote_verbatim: which one has the same footprint
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Board-to-board connectors for compute modules became unobtainable in 2021 and 2022, and were found only by canvassing industry contacts and forums outside normal distribution channels.
claims.quote_verbatim: We can't get these Hiroshi connectors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Moving Down The Stack with Scott Williams

claims.claim_text: A design house can supply scarce components to a client's manufacturer as free-issue material so that a build can continue, which shifts part of the sourcing burden back up to the designer.
claims.quote_verbatim: we would then supply those components
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Moving Down The Stack with Scott Williams

claims.claim_text: Distributor stock is not production stock: ten instances of a part on each of a thousand boards exceeds what a catalogue distributor holds, at which point parts must be bought as reels direct from the manufacturer.
claims.quote_verbatim: DigiKey is actually not enough volume. So you start buying reels from the manufacturer
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Moving Down The Stack with Scott Williams

claims.claim_text: A single missing line item stops an entire production line, so a bill of materials has to be complete rather than mostly available.
claims.quote_verbatim: One part will hold up an entire production line
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Passive component quality cannot be verified by the buyer, since establishing a capacitor's endurance would require thousands of hours of stress testing per batch, so selection rests on manufacturer reputation and trust in the seller.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to do it based on your knowledge of the industry and the trust that has been built up in certain manufacturers
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Part selection can be risk-tiered by duty: unbranded low-cost silicon is acceptable in an unstressed battery-powered design, while components operating near their limits are restricted to manufacturers with a known record.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I know I've got some product where those components are going to be stressed, I am only going to trust the name brands
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: LCSC is an authorised distributor for the brands it lists and does not substitute parts, so a buyer receives the genuine device even when it is an unfamiliar Asian brand; consumer marketplaces such as AliExpress carry no such guarantee.
claims.quote_verbatim: they are an official supplier for those brands, just like Mouser and DigiKey are
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Turnkey services from Chinese board houses are cheaper again when the design uses their suggested parts, because those reels are already loaded in the pick-and-place machines.
claims.quote_verbatim: they've already got those reels, you know, lined up in their pick-and-place machines
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The turnkey route only suits designs whose components are generic; a precision instrument using 0.05 percent resistors and specific amplifiers has no substitution latitude and cannot be built from a house parts library.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't substitute the parts in that, right? They're all precision
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: In a robot bill of materials the actuation hardware dominates: motors and motor controllers alone accounted for roughly eighty percent of cost, so switching those two line items to Chinese suppliers produced a two-thousand-dollar reduction even with tariffs applied.
claims.quote_verbatim: probably is around like, you know, 80% of your, your bomb costs
claims.speaker: Aaed Musa

claims.claim_text: Enterprise resource planning for hardware ties design data to purchasing and receiving, so that components are ordered against forecast builds and their arrival dates are tracked; the established systems are priced for large companies, with customisation of a major package running to about a million dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're spending a million dollars to customize it
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty
claims.episode_title: AI Tooling with Matt Liberty and Luke Beno

claims.claim_text: Parts held at a contract manufacturer can go missing without a tracking system, so an inventory system is used to record where each part physically is as well as how many there are.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had an issue over the last few years where parts kind of went missing
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty
claims.episode_title: AI Tooling with Matt Liberty and Luke Beno
